articleTitle: Photometry and the testing of incandescent lamps
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: At one time photometry was regarded merely as an interesting and fascinating study for the professor in the laboratory. To-day it is a process of industrial importance. New illuminants have come to the fore and new methods of employing them are constantly being devised — and how can we compare their merits without measuring the light derived from them? Whatever be the method of lighting adopted, it is the illumination derived from it with which we are concerned and for which we pay. Measurement of this commodity would therefore seem to be an elementary safeguard to be observed in any contract relating to the sale of light.

articleTitle: Valedictory address
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: Mr. President and Gentlemen, two years ago this Institute made an important change in its Constitution. At a Special General Meeting, held on the 28th of January, 1926, it was decided to raise the standard of qualifications necessary for admission to associate membership of the Institute. Since then the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers has taken its place in the rank of the leading engineering societies in England and America. The main object of this alteration to the Constitution was to secure for South African electrical engineers the recognition for purposes of appointment and promotion which they justly deserved, and which had until then, at least on the part of some of our employers, been given to those who possessed associate membership in the English Institute of Electrical Engineers.

articleTitle: “The rating of incandescent lamps and their accessories”
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: I wish to confine most of my remarks to the subject of glare. There is one cause of . glare in lamps which does not appear to have been discussed very much, and which is produced by reflection from certain regions of the glass bulb. I do not refer to the ordinary thin reflection of the filament which one can generally observe, but to the caustic effect or partial flashing-over of part of the bulb, so that light is collected and reflected to the eye from a comparatively large area. When the bulb is viewed from certain directions, this partial flashing-over gives rise to bands of brightness in space, and these bands must necessarily cause a diminution of illumination in other directions. The net result is to give a peaked curve of candle-power distribution.

articleTitle: Notes on the electric plant of a rand gold mine in 1896
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: It has been suggested that any improvement of the electrical plants on our mines should be recorded in the Transactions of the Institute of Electrical Engineers. This will no doubt prove helpful to many members. For comparison it might be interesting to look back thirty-two years. I have therefore penned a few notes concerning the electric plant of an important mine in 1896. At that time I believe direct current only was used on practically all the gold mines of the Witwatersrand, the voltage ranging from 110 to 550, the latter being considered rather a high voltage. The electric plant of the mine in question consisted of two “lirge” direct current generators, each of 550 volts 250 amperes capacity, two lighting generators of 110 volts 165 amperes, and two direct current rotary transformers 550/110 volts 200 amperes secondary, and about 25 motors ranging from 10 h.p. to 80 h.p., as well as one “large” motor of 120 h.p.

abstract: The. severe loading conditions existing in modern power systems, involving very great and rapid fluctuation of load, have fostered the growth of the automatic voltage regulator. As the characteristic of an alternator resembles that of an ordinary direct-current shunt wound generator, in that the terminal voltage falls with increase of load, it is essential that some device be fitted which will automatically increase the excitation of the alternator as the load increases, so that the terminal voltage may remain constant, or even rise with increase of current.
